First listed 2025-06-06 · episode or wrap

Stablecoin and Instability with Trump and Musk - The Friday Market Wrap!

Eisman remains cautious despite the market rebound, arguing that unresolved trade negotiations can still produce a bad outcome. He expects more dedicated nuclear-power deals, explains the Wells Fargo asset cap, and discusses Bitcoin and stablecoins. He is less skeptical of Bitcoin than before but has not invested and doubts its behavior as a hedge.

YouTube · 2025-06-06 ↗Substack · 2025-06-07 ↗
The forecast of more nuclear arrangements is supported by later deals. His insistence on separating a stablecoin business from a speculative token is useful. Macro assurance that only a trade war could disrupt growth is too sweeping, and his apparent contradiction between jobs headlines confuses different comparison baselines.

How he reasons here

  • A lack of immediate bad results does not eliminate latent risk.
  • Follow physical infrastructure commitments behind AI enthusiasm.
  • Understand regulatory constraints before extrapolating bank growth.
  • Distinguish an asset narrative from observed return behavior.
  • Separate a payment network from a token issuer business.
